Source: step 2 of the selected node's supplied proof (parent 2(b): zero-scale currents are minimizing), together with its (0f) (uniqueness of weak limits). Simon 7.3.3, proof of (1), (8) (chapter-07.txt lines 443–462): weak limits of η_{x_i,λ_i#}T with λ_i → 0 minimize in all of ℝ^{n+ℓ}. Only hypothesis (MB) is used.
1. Apply (MB) to n, k, ℓ, U, N, T (with the given hypotheses), the point x ∈ U, the centres xs := (x_i), the scales lams := (λ_i) with their positivity proofs, and the convergences x_i → x, λ_i → 0. It yields a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ and C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^{n+k}) with ConvergesWeakly (j ↦ blowUp T x_{φ(j)} λ_{φ(j)}) C, IsMinimizingIn C univ and BoundaryVanishes C. The MassMeasuresConverge part is not needed.
2. Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^{n+k}) (TestFormOn univ n) and put a_i := currentEval (blowUp T x_i λ_i) ω. By hypothesis, a_i → S ω. Since φ is strictly increasing, φ(j) → ∞ (StrictMono.tendsto_atTop), so a_{φ(j)} → S ω (Tendsto.comp). The sequence of step 1 evaluated at ω is literally j ↦ a_{φ(j)}, so a_{φ(j)} → C ω. Limits in ℝ are unique (tendsto_nhds_unique), hence S ω = C ω.
3. As ω was arbitrary, S = C (GeometricCurrentOn.ext).
4. Rewriting the conclusions of step 1 with S = C gives IsMinimizingIn S univ and BoundaryVanishes S. ∎
proof_key_steps: Apply (MB) at the limit point x ∈ U of the centres: a subsequence of the blow-ups converges weakly to some C minimizing in ℝ^{n+k} with ∂C = 0.
Weak limits are unique: along φ the evaluations converge both to S ω and to C ω, so S = C by GeometricCurrentOn.ext.
Transfer IsMinimizingIn univ and BoundaryVanishes from C to S.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: (0h) of the selected node's supplied proof (vanishing blow-ups), with the choice of ε made explicit from the definition of the support (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn.support = U ∖ zeroRegion, Simon 6.2.11). Only part (ii) of (BC) is used.
Notation: for λ > 0, η_{p,λ} := dilation p λ, so η_{p,λ}(v) = −(λ⁻¹•p) + λ⁻¹•v = b + L v with L := dilationCLM P λ and b := −(λ⁻¹•p).
1. (Choice of ε.) By definition spt T = U ∖ zeroRegion T, where zeroRegion T is the union of all open W with closure W compact, closure W ⊆ U and T.VanishesOn W. As p ∈ U and p ∉ spt T, p lies in such a W. Since W is open, there is ε > 0 with B_ε(p) ⊆ W (Metric.isOpen_iff). Then B_ε(p) ⊆ W ⊆ closure W ⊆ U.
2. (Vanishing.) If ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) has tsupport ω ⊆ B_ε(p), then tsupport ω ⊆ W, so T ω = 0 because T.VanishesOn W. Thus T.VanishesOn (B_ε(p)).
3. (Mass.) T.massOn (B_ε(p)) is the supremum in [0, ∞] of ofReal(T ω) over the admissible forms ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (massAdmissibleOn U n (B_ε(p))), each of which has tsupport ω ⊆ B_ε(p). By step 2 each value is ofReal 0 = 0, so the supremum is 0 (sSup_le, and 0 ≤ anything).
4. (Weak convergence.) Let λ_j > 0 with λ_j → 0 and let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P). Its topological support is compact (HasCompactSupport), hence bounded: there is R_ω > 0 with tsupport ω ⊆ B_{R_ω}(0). Since λ_j R_ω → 0, there is j₀ with λ_j R_ω < ε for all j ≥ j₀.
5. Fix j ≥ j₀ and put λ := λ_j. By (BC)(ii), applied to T, p, λ and the underlying form of ω, currentEval (blowUp T p λ) ω = currentEval T ω′ with ω′ := affinePullbackForm L b ω.
6. By tsupport_affinePullbackForm_subset, tsupport ω′ ⊆ (v ↦ b + L v)⁻¹(tsupport ω) = η_{p,λ}⁻¹(tsupport ω) ⊆ η_{p,λ}⁻¹(B_{R_ω}(0)). Since ‖η_{p,λ}(v)‖ = λ⁻¹‖v − p‖, η_{p,λ}⁻¹(B_{R_ω}(0)) = B_{λR_ω}(p) ⊆ B_ε(p).
7. By definition, currentEval T ω′ equals T⟨ω′, h⟩ if h : IsTestForm ω′ ∧ tsupport ω′ ⊆ U holds, and 0 otherwise. In the first case ⟨ω′, h⟩ ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) has tsupport ⊆ B_ε(p) (step 6), so the value is 0 by step 2. In both cases currentEval T ω′ = 0.
8. Hence currentEval (blowUp T p λ_j) ω = 0 for all j ≥ j₀. The sequence is eventually equal to the constant 0 = (0 : GeometricCurrentOn univ n) ω (GeometricCurrentOn.zero_apply), so it tends to it (tendsto_const_nhds.congr' with an eventual equality). As ω was arbitrary, ConvergesWeakly (j ↦ blowUp T p λ_j) 0.
Steps 1, 2, 3 and 8 give all four conclusions. ∎
proof_key_steps: p ∈ U ∖ spt T lies in an open W with compact closure in U on which T vanishes; choose B_ε(p) ⊆ W.
T vanishes on B_ε(p), so every admissible form gives ofReal 0 and M_{B_ε(p)}(T) = 0.

For a test form ω with tsupport ω ⊆ B_{R_ω}(0), (BC)(ii) turns blowUp T p λ(ω) into T applied to the pulled-back form, whose support lies in B_{λR_ω}(p) ⊆ B_ε(p) once λR_ω < ε; so the values are eventually 0.

1. (Domain.) η is surjective: η(y + λu) = −λ⁻¹•y + λ⁻¹•y + u = u for every u. Hence η(ℝ^P) = ℝ^P; in particular univ ⊆ η '' univ.
2. (Definition of S′.) Put S′ := B.restrictDomain h, with h : univ ⊆ η '' univ from step 1. For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P), S′ ω = B(testFormOnInclusion h n ω) (restrictDomain_apply), and testFormOnInclusion does not change the underlying form. Since ω is a test form with tsupport ω ⊆ η(ℝ^P), the definition of currentEval (dif_pos) gives currentEval B ω = B(testFormOnInclusion h n ω) = S′ ω.
3. (Pulled-back forms are test forms on ℝ^P.) Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) and ω′ := affinePullbackForm L b ω. The map v ↦ b + L v = η is a homeomorphism of ℝ^P (multiplication by λ⁻¹ ≠ 0 followed by a translation), hence proper (Homeomorph.isProperMap). By affinePullbackForm_isTestForm, ω′ is a test form; trivially tsupport ω′ ⊆ ℝ^P. So ω′ defines an element of 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P).
4. (Evaluations.) Fix i. (BC)(iii), applied to T, x := c_i, lam := t_i, y and mu := λ, gives currentEval (blowUp (blowUp T c_i t_i) y λ) ω = currentEval (blowUp T (c_i + t_i•y) (t_iλ)) ω. (BC)(ii), applied to the current blowUp T c_i t_i ∈ 𝒟_n(dilation c_i t_i '' U), x := y and lam := λ, gives currentEval (blowUp (blowUp T c_i t_i) y λ) ω = currentEval (blowUp T c_i t_i) ω′. Hence currentEval (blowUp T (c_i + t_i•y) (t_iλ)) ω = currentEval (blowUp T c_i t_i) ω′ for every i. (The proofs that t_iλ ≠ 0 used in (BC)(iii) and in the statement are proofs of the same proposition, so the currents coincide by proof irrelevance.)
5. (Convergence.) The hypothesis, applied to the test form ω′ of step 3, gives currentEval (blowUp T c_i t_i) ω′ → S⟨ω′, _⟩ = currentEval S ω′ (dif_pos). By (BC)(ii) applied to S, y, λ: currentEval B ω = currentEval S ω′, and currentEval B ω = S′ ω by step 2. With step 4, currentEval (blowUp T (c_i + t_i•y) (t_iλ)) ω → S′ ω. As ω was arbitrary, blowUp T (c_i + t_i•y) (t_iλ) ⇀ S′ in ℝ^P.
6. (IMRep of S′.) Let R be an IMRep of S in ℝ^P. (BUI), applied to S, y, λ and R, gives an IMRep R₁ in η(ℝ^P) representing B with R₁.measure(s) = ofReal(λ⁻¹ⁿ)·R.measure(η⁻¹(s)) for every Borel s. Every field of IMRep transfers: the domain only enters through carrier ⊆ domain (trivial for univ) and through compact K ⊆ domain in locallyIntegrable_mult, where K ⊆ univ = η(univ) by step 1. Since IMRep.action and IMRep.measure only use carrier, mult and orient, R′.action = R₁.action and R′.measure = R₁.measure. Source: steps 3 and 4 of the selected node's supplied proof (parent 3(iii); Simon 7.3.3, proof of (1), and Remark 3.4 — the measures of 𝒯 are θ·Hⁿ, chapter-07.txt lines 443–486). The parent's positive-scale parameters (x, λ) are written (a, t) = (z + rx, rλ) and its zero-scale data (x_i, λ_i, x̄) are written (c_i, t_i, b) = (z + rx_i, rλ_i, z + rx̄). Step 4(a) of the supplied proof is exactly the reused sibling density_representation (Submission.idtp_fons_cc_density_representation). For positive-scale members, steps 4(b)–(c) are replaced by an equivalent route: μ_{a,t} is exhibited as the weight of an integer multiplicity representation (restriction to W by the reused sibling imrep_restrict, Submission.dor_lmb_imrep_restrict_current, then blow-up by (BUI)), to which 4(a) applies. This avoids transporting Hⁿ-a.e. statements through η. Siblings used: ambient_calculus (Submission.idtp_fons_cc_ambient_calculus) part (2), density_representation, imrep_restrict.
Notation: Hⁿ := μHE[n], ω_n := unitBallVolume n, μ_T := RT.measure, W := B_{2r}(z).
1. (IMRep weights are finite on compact subsets of the domain.) Let R be an IMRep in a set V and K ⊆ V compact. K is closed, hence Borel. By definition R.measure = (Hⁿ⌞R.carrier).withDensity(R.mult), so R.measure(K) = ∫⁻_K R.mult d(Hⁿ⌞R.carrier) (withDensity_apply) = ∫⁻_{R.carrier ∩ K} R.mult dHⁿ (Measure.restrict_restrict, Set.inter_comm), which is ≠ ∞ by the field locallyIntegrable_mult. In particular μ_T(B̄_{2r}(z)) ≠ ∞, as B̄_{2r}(z) is compact (isCompact_closedBall) and contained in U; hence μ_T(W) ≤ μ_T(B̄_{2r}(z)) < ∞ (ball_subset_closedBall, measure_mono).
2. (Property (1).) Let μ ∈ 𝓜 and K ⊆ ℝ^{n+k} compact. By the class hypothesis μ is (PS) or (ZS).
 (PS) μ = ofReal(t⁻¹ⁿ) • (μ_T⌞W).map(dilation a t) with t > 0. By ambient_calculus (2) with A := univ, μ(univ) = ofReal(t⁻¹ⁿ)·(μ_T⌞W)((dilation a t)⁻¹(univ)) = ofReal(t⁻¹ⁿ)·μ_T(W) (Measure.restrict_apply_univ), a product of two finite elements of [0, ∞] (step 1; ENNReal.mul_ne_top). Hence μ(K) ≤ μ(univ) < ∞ (measure_mono).
 (ZS) μ = RS.measure with RS an IMRep in ℝ^{n+k}; K ⊆ univ, so μ(K) ≠ ∞ by step 1.
3. ((DEM) from (DEN).) Let P, n ∈ ℕ, V ⊆ ℝ^P and let R be an IMRep in V with R.measure(K) ≠ ∞ for every compact K. Apply (DEN) to R with W := univ (isOpen_univ); its hypothesis R.measure(K ∩ univ) ≠ ∞ holds because K ∩ univ = K. Rewriting B_ρ(x) ∩ univ = B_ρ(x) and R.carrier ∩ univ = R.carrier (Set.inter_univ), its conclusion reads: for μHE[n]-a.e. x, R.measure(B_ρ(x))/(ω_n·ofReal(ρⁿ)) → 1_{R.carrier}(x)·R.mult(x) as ρ → 0⁺. This is exactly the leading hypothesis (DEM) of density_representation (its premise 1 ≤ n is not even needed).
4. (Density representation of IMRep weights.) Let R be an IMRep in some V ⊆ ℝ^{n+k} whose weight is finite on every compact set. density_representation, applied to (DEM) of step 3, to R and to 1 ≤ n, gives R.measure = Hⁿ.withDensity(x ↦ ofReal((limsup_{ρ→0⁺} R.measure(B_ρ(x))/(ω_n·ofReal(ρⁿ))).toReal)). By the defining equation of dens, the integrand is x ↦ ofReal(dens R.measure x). Hence R.measure = Hⁿ.withDensity(x ↦ ofReal(dens R.measure x)).
5. (Property (2), zero-scale members.) If μ = RS.measure, then RS.measure is finite on compact sets by step 2, and step 4 (with V = univ) gives (2) for μ.
6. (Property (2), positive-scale members.) Let μ = ofReal(t⁻¹ⁿ) • (μ_T⌞W).map η with η := dilation a t and t > 0.
 (a) imrep_restrict, applied to U (open), A := W (an open ball, hence Borel: measurableSet_ball) and RT, gives S_W ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and an IMRep R_W in U representing S_W with R_W.measure = μ_T⌞W.
 (b) (BUI), applied to S_W, a, t and R_W, gives an IMRep R″ in η(U) = dilation a t '' U representing blowUp S_W a t with R″.measure(s) = ofReal(t⁻¹ⁿ)·R_W.measure(η⁻¹(s)) for every Borel s.
 (c) For Borel s, ambient_calculus (2) gives μ(s) = ofReal(t⁻¹ⁿ)·(μ_T⌞W)(η⁻¹(s)) = ofReal(t⁻¹ⁿ)·R_W.measure(η⁻¹(s)) = R″.measure(s). By Measure.ext, R″.measure = μ.
 (d) Hence R″.measure is finite on compact sets (step 2), and step 4 (with V := η(U)) gives R″.measure = Hⁿ.withDensity(x ↦ ofReal(dens R″.measure x)). Rewriting R″.measure = μ everywhere gives (2) for μ.
7. Steps 2, 5 and 6 prove (1) and (2). ∎

Siblings used: ambient_calculus (Submission.idtp_fons_cc_ambient_calculus) part (7), and zero_limit_rescale (Submission.dimred_tr_bc_zero_limit_rescale), applied with (BC) and (BUI).
Let μ ∈ 𝓜, y ∈ ℝ^{n+k}, 0 < λ < 1 and ‖y‖ ≤ 1 − λ, and put μ′ := ofReal(λ⁻¹ⁿ) • μ.map(dilation y λ). By the class hypothesis, μ is (PS) or (ZS).
1. (Triangle inequality.) For s ≥ 0 and c ∈ ℝ^{n+k}: dist(c + s•y, z) = ‖(c − z) + s•y‖ ≤ dist(c, z) + ‖s•y‖ = dist(c, z) + s‖y‖ ≤ dist(c, z) + s(1 − λ).
2. (Case PS.) μ = ofReal(t⁻¹ⁿ) • (μ_T⌞W).map(dilation a t) with 0 < t ≤ r and dist(a, z) ≤ r − t. ambient_calculus (7), with ν := μ_T⌞W, s := t and t := λ, gives μ′ = ofReal((tλ)⁻¹ⁿ) • (μ_T⌞W).map(dilation (a + t•y) (tλ)). The pair (a + t•y, tλ) is admissible: tλ > 0; tλ ≤ t ≤ r because λ < 1; and dist(a + t•y, z) ≤ (r − t) + t(1 − λ) = r − tλ by step 1. So μ′ is (PS), and μ′ ∈ 𝓜 by the class hypothesis.
3. (Case ZS.) μ = RS.measure, where RS is an IMRep of S in ℝ^{n+k} and (c_i, t_i, b) are zero-scale data for S (with positivity proofs hts). Apply zero_limit_rescale with (BC), (BUI), P := n + k, U, T, cs := (c_i), ts := (t_i), hts, S, y, λ and the convergence blowUp T c_i t_i ⇀ S. It gives S′ ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^{n+k}) with blowUp T (c_i + t_i•y) (t_iλ) ⇀ S′ and, for RS, an IMRep RS′ of S′ in ℝ^{n+k} with RS′.measure = μ′.
4. The data c′_i := c_i + t_i•y, t′_i := t_iλ (positivity proofs mul_pos (hts i) hλ) and b′ := b are zero-scale data for S′:
 (a) dist(c′_i, z) ≤ dist(c_i, z) + t_i(1 − λ) < (r − t_i) + t_i(1 − λ) = r − t′_i (step 1);
 (b) t_iλ → 0·λ = 0 (Tendsto.mul_const);
 (c) c_i + t_i•y → b + 0•y = b (Tendsto.add, Tendsto.smul_const);
 (d) blowUp T c′_i t′_i ⇀ S′ is the convergence of step 3 (the same currents).

proof_key_steps: Positive scale: ambient_calculus (7) gives (μ_T⌞W)^{a,t} rescaled by (y, λ) = (μ_T⌞W)^{a+ty,tλ}, and (a + ty, tλ) is admissible by the triangle inequality.

The new data satisfy dist(c_i + t_i y, z) < r − t_iλ, t_iλ → 0 and c_i + t_i y → b, so the rescaled measure is a zero-scale member.

P2. (Integrals against rescaled measures.) For a measure m on E, a ∈ E, s > 0 and continuous f: ∫ f dm^{a,s} = s⁻ⁿ·∫ f∘(dilation a s) dm. Indeed (ofReal(s⁻¹ⁿ)).toReal = s⁻ⁿ (integral_smul_measure), and dilation a s is continuous, so integral_map applies (f is continuous, hence AEStronglyMeasurable).
P3. (Support of f∘η.) If tsupport f ⊆ B_{R_f}(0) and η := dilation a s with s > 0, then f(η(v)) ≠ 0 implies v ∈ η⁻¹(B_{R_f}(0)) = B_{sR_f}(a) (ambient_calculus (3) with w = 0). Every continuous f with compact support admits such an R_f > 0 (compact sets are bounded).
P4. (The zero member.) Let R_∅ be the IMRep in E with carrier ∅, multiplicity 0 and orientation 0. Its fields hold: ∅ is Borel and ∅ ⊆ E; ∅ is countably n-rectifiable (countablyRectifiable_of_measure_zero, Hⁿ(∅) = 0); mult_pos is vacuous; lower integrals over ∅ are 0 ≠ ∞; Hⁿ⌞∅ = 0, so the two a.e. fields hold trivially. R_∅.action ω = ∫_∅ … = 0 = (0 : GeometricCurrentOn univ n) ω, so R_∅ represents 0, and R_∅.measure = (Hⁿ⌞∅).withDensity 0 = 0. The zero measure is n-homogeneous: 0((v ↦ λv)(s)) = 0 = ofReal(λⁿ)·0.
P5. (E as ambient manifold.) ambient_calculus (1) gives IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 (n + k) univ; also (closure univ ∖ univ) ∩ univ = ∅, univ ∩ univ = univ, IsOpen univ, k ≤ k and spt S ⊆ univ. Hence (TAN) (with ℓ := k and U = N = univ) applies to every S ∈ 𝒟_n(E) that is minimizing in E with ∂S = 0, at every point of spt S.
P6. (Zero-scale data.) If (c_i, t_i, b) are zero-scale data for S (dist(c_i, z) < r − t_i, t_i → 0, c_i → b, blowUp T c_i t_i ⇀ S), then dist(b, z) ≤ r (dist(c_i, z) ≤ r for all i and dist(·, z) is continuous: le_of_tendsto), so b ∈ B̄_r(z) ⊆ K ⊆ U. zero_limit_minimizing (with (MB), the hypotheses of T and x := b) shows that S is minimizing in E and ∂S = 0.
P7. (IMReps of blow-ups.) For a current A on a domain O with an IMRep R, a ∈ E and s > 0, (BUI) gives an IMRep R′ in dilation a s '' O representing blowUp A a s with R′.measure(B) = ofReal(s⁻¹ⁿ)·R.measure((dilation a s)⁻¹(B)) for Borel B. The measure (R.measure)^{a,s} is given on Borel sets by the same formula (Measure.smul_apply, Measure.map_apply; dilation is measurable), so R′.measure = (R.measure)^{a,s} (Measure.ext).
P8. (Mass bound for (IBL).) Apply (MON) to T with d := n + ℓ (1 ≤ n ≤ n + ℓ ≤ n + k) and part (i) to the compact K ⊆ U: there is Λ_K ≥ 0 such that τ ↦ ofReal(e^{Λ_Kτ}/τⁿ)·M_{B_τ(c′)}(T) is monotone on (0, R′) whenever B̄_{R′}(c′) ⊆ K. Let b ∈ B̄_r(z), δ := r/4, Γ′ := ofReal(e^{Λ_K r/4}/(r/4)ⁿ)·μ_T(W) (finite by P1) and Γ := Γ′.toReal. Let x′ ∈ B_δ(b) and 0 < ρ < δ. Then dist(x′, z) < 5r/4, so B̄_{r/2}(x′) ⊆ K and B_{r/4}(x′) ⊆ W ⊆ U. Monotonicity on (0, r/2), at ρ < r/4, gives ofReal(e^{Λ_Kρ}/ρⁿ)·M_{B_ρ(x′)}(T) ≤ ofReal(e^{Λ_K r/4}/(r/4)ⁿ)·M_{B_{r/4}(x′)}(T) ≤ Γ′, because M_{B_{r/4}(x′)}(T) = μ_T(B_{r/4}(x′)) ≤ μ_T(W) (P1). As e^{Λ_Kρ} ≥ 1, ofReal(1/ρⁿ)·M_{B_ρ(x′)}(T) ≤ Γ′, so M_{B_ρ(x′)}(T) ≤ ofReal(ρⁿ)·Γ′ = ofReal(Γρⁿ). Thus the mass hypothesis of (IBL) holds at b with (δ, Γ).
P9. (Tails and parameter congruence.) If evaluations converge along a sequence, they converge along each tail j ↦ j + j₀ (Tendsto.comp with tendsto_add_atTop_nat); so ConvergesWeakly passes to tails. Blow-ups with equal centres and scales are equal currents (the nonvanishing proofs are irrelevant).
Main argument. Let μ ∈ 𝓜, y ∈ E with ‖y‖ < 1, and λ_j > 0 strictly decreasing with λ_j → 0 (only λ_j > 0 and λ_j → 0 are used). By the class hypothesis μ is (PS) or (ZS).
1. Case (PS): μ = (μ_T⌞W)^{a,t} with 0 < t ≤ r and dist(a, z) ≤ r − t. Put p := a + t•y.
 (a) By ambient_calculus (7), μ^{y,s} = (μ_T⌞W)^{p,ts} for every s > 0.
 (b) dist(p, z) ≤ dist(a, z) + t‖y‖ ≤ r − t + t‖y‖ < r. Put d := r − dist(p, z) > 0. Then p ∈ B_r(z) ⊆ U, and B_ρ(p) ⊆ W for every ρ ≤ r.
 (c) Choose j₀ with tλ_j < d for all j ≥ j₀ (λ_j → 0).
 Case (PS-i): p ∈ spt T. Apply (TAN) to T (with its hypotheses) at x := p with the scales tλ_j > 0 (tλ_j → 0). It gives a strictly increasing φ and C ∈ 𝒟_n(E) with blowUp T p (tλ_{φ(j)}) ⇀ C, MassMeasuresConverge for the same sequence, C minimizing in E, and n-homogeneous weights for every IMRep of C. C is integer multiplicity (the first conjunct of IsMinimizingIn); fix an IMRep R_C of C in E and put ν := R_C.measure, sub := φ.
 – ν ∈ 𝓜: c′_j := p, t′_j := tλ_{φ(j+j₀)} and b′ := p are zero-scale data for C. Indeed φ(j + j₀) ≥ j + j₀ ≥ j₀ (StrictMono.id_le), so t′_j < d, i.e. dist(p, z) < r − t′_j; t′_j → 0; the constant sequence tends to p; and blowUp T p t′_j ⇀ C by P9. As R_C represents C, the class hypothesis gives ν ∈ 𝓜.
 – Homogeneity of ν is the last conclusion of (TAN), applied to R_C.
 – Convergence: let f be continuous with compact support, tsupport f ⊆ B_{R_f}(0). Let R_j be the IMRep of blowUp T p (tλ_{φ(j)}) given by P7 from RT, so R_j.measure = μ_T^{p,tλ_{φ(j)}}. MassMeasuresConverge, applied to (R_j), R_C, f and tsupport f ⊆ univ, gives ∫ f dR_j.measure → ∫ f dν. For every j with tλ_{φ(j)}R_f < r (all large j), put η := dilation p (tλ_{φ(j)}). By P2 and (a), ∫ f dμ^{y,λ_{φ(j)}} = (tλ_{φ(j)})⁻ⁿ ∫ f∘η d(μ_T⌞W) and ∫ f dR_j.measure = (tλ_{φ(j)})⁻ⁿ ∫ f∘η dμ_T. By P3 and (b), f∘η vanishes outside B_{tλ_{φ(j)}R_f}(p) ⊆ W, so ∫ f∘η d(μ_T⌞W) = ∫ f∘η dμ_T (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero). The two sequences agree eventually, hence ∫ f dμ^{y,λ_{φ(j)}} → ∫ f dν (Tendsto.congr').
 Case (PS-ii): p ∉ spt T. As p ∈ U, vanishing_blowup (with (BC)) gives ε > 0 with B_ε(p) ⊆ U, M_{B_ε(p)}(T) = 0 and blowUp T p s_j ⇀ 0 for every sequence s_j > 0 with s_j → 0. By P1, μ_T(B_ε(p)) = 0. Put ν := 0 = R_∅.measure (P4) and sub := id.
 – ν ∈ 𝓜: c′_j := p, t′_j := tλ_{j+j₀} and b′ := p are zero-scale data for the zero current: dist(p, z) < r − t′_j by (c); t′_j → 0; c′_j → p; and blowUp T p t′_j ⇀ 0 by vanishing_blowup. As R_∅ represents 0, 0 ∈ 𝓜.
 – ν = 0 is homogeneous (P4).
 – Convergence: for f as above and j with tλ_jR_f < ε, put η := dilation p (tλ_j). By P2 and (a), ∫ f dμ^{y,λ_j} = (tλ_j)⁻ⁿ ∫ f∘η d(μ_T⌞W). By P3, f∘η vanishes outside B_ε(p), which is μ_T-null and hence (μ_T⌞W)-null, so f∘η = 0 a.e. and the integral is 0 (integral_eq_zero_of_ae). The sequence is eventually 0, so it tends to 0 = ∫ f d0 (integral_zero_measure).
2. Case (ZS): μ = RS.measure, RS an IMRep of S in E, with zero-scale data (c_i, t_i, b). By P6, S is minimizing in E with ∂S = 0, and b ∈ B̄_r(z) ⊆ U. By P8, the mass hypothesis of (IBL) holds at b.
 Case (ZS-i): y ∈ spt S. By P5, (TAN) applies to S at y with the scales λ_j: it gives a strictly increasing φ and C ∈ 𝒟_n(E) with blowUp S y λ_{φ(j)} ⇀ C, MassMeasuresConverge for the same sequence, C minimizing in E, and n-homogeneous weights. Fix an IMRep R_C of C; ν := R_C.measure, sub := φ.
 – Convergence: by P7 (A := S, R := RS), the IMRep R′_j of blowUp S y λ_{φ(j)} has weight RS.measure^{y,λ_{φ(j)}} = μ^{y,λ_{φ(j)}}. MassMeasuresConverge, applied to (R′_j), R_C, f and tsupport f ⊆ univ, gives ∫ f dμ^{y,λ_{φ(j)}} → ∫ f dν.
 – Homogeneity of ν: the last conclusion of (TAN).
 – ν ∈ 𝓜: apply (IBL) with P := n + k, U (open), T, x := b ∈ U, xs := (c_i), lams := (t_i), S, y, ss := (λ_{φ(k)}) (positive, → 0) and C. Its hypotheses are c_i → b, t_i → 0, λ_{φ(k)} → 0, the mass bound of P8, blowUp T c_i t_i ⇀ S and blowUp S y λ_{φ(k)} ⇀ C. It yields a strictly increasing φ′ with blowUp T (c_{φ′(k)} + t_{φ′(k)}•y) (t_{φ′(k)}λ_{φ(k)}) ⇀ C. Since λ_{φ(k)} → 0 and 1 − ‖y‖ > 0, choose k₀ with λ_{φ(k)} ≤ 1 − ‖y‖ for all k ≥ k₀. Put i(k) := φ′(k + k₀), c″_k := c_{i(k)} + t_{i(k)}•y, t″_k := t_{i(k)}λ_{φ(k+k₀)} > 0 and b″ := b. These are zero-scale data for C: dist(c″_k, z) ≤ dist(c_{i(k)}, z) + t_{i(k)}‖y‖ < (r − t_{i(k)}) + t_{i(k)}(1 − λ_{φ(k+k₀)}) = r − t″_k; t″_k → 0 (a product of two sequences tending to 0); c″_k → b + 0•y = b; and blowUp T c″_k t″_k ⇀ C by P9. As R_C represents C, ν ∈ 𝓜.
 Case (ZS-ii): y ∉ spt S. vanishing_blowup, applied to S (domain univ, y ∈ univ), gives ε > 0 with M_{B_ε(y)}(S) = 0 and blowUp S y s_k ⇀ 0 for every sequence s_k > 0 with s_k → 0. By (IM)(a) for S (univ open, RS represents S), μ(B_ε(y)) = RS.measure(B_ε(y)) = M_{B_ε(y)}(S) = 0. Put ν := 0 = R_∅.measure and sub := id.
 – ν ∈ 𝓜: apply (IBL) as in (ZS-i), now with ss := (λ_k), C := 0 and blowUp S y λ_k ⇀ 0. With k₀ such that λ_k ≤ 1 − ‖y‖ for all k ≥ k₀, the data c″_k := c_{φ′(k+k₀)} + t_{φ′(k+k₀)}•y, t″_k := t_{φ′(k+k₀)}λ_{k+k₀} and b are zero-scale data for 0 (same estimates), and R_∅ represents 0. So 0 ∈ 𝓜.
 – ν = 0 is homogeneous (P4).
 – Convergence: for f with tsupport f ⊆ B_{R_f}(0) and λ_jR_f < ε, P2 gives ∫ f dμ^{y,λ_j} = λ_j⁻ⁿ ∫ f∘(dilation y λ_j) dμ, and by P3 the integrand vanishes outside the μ-null set B_ε(y). So the integrals are eventually 0, and they tend to 0 = ∫ f d0.
3. In every case sub is strictly increasing, ν ∈ 𝓜, ν is n-homogeneous, and ∫ f dμ^{y,λ_{sub(j)}} → ∫ f dν for every continuous compactly supported f. ∎
proof_key_steps: Preliminaries: mass equals weight on open sets ((IM)(a)), integrals against rescaled measures, the zero IMRep, ℝ^{n+k} as ambient manifold, minimality of zero-scale limits (zero_limit_minimizing), IMReps of blow-ups ((BUI)), and the mass bound required by (IBL) from (MON)(i).

Positive-scale member, p = a + ty ∈ spt T: (TAN) at p with scales tλ_j gives a homogeneous minimizing tangent limit C; its weight is a zero-scale member (constant centres p) and the vague limit, since the rescaled member and the IMRep weight of the blow-up agree on test functions supported in B_{2r}(z).
Positive-scale member with p ∉ spt T: vanishing_blowup gives blow-ups ⇀ 0 and a μ_T-null ball, so ν = 0 = R_∅.measure works.

Zero-scale member, y ∈ spt S: (TAN) for S at y gives C and vague convergence via MassMeasuresConverge; (IBL) plus a tail argument shows C is again a zero-scale limit of blow-ups of T, so its weight lies in 𝓜.
Zero-scale member with y ∉ spt S: vanishing_blowup and (IBL) with C = 0 show 0 ∈ 𝓜, and the rescaled integrals vanish eventually.

(These are the selected node's positive-scale members μ_{x,λ} and zero-scale members, with (a, t) = (z + rx, rλ), c_i = z + rx_i, t_i = rλ_i, b = z + rx̄.) Then there is Λ ∈ ℝ such that for every μ ∈ 𝓜, every y ∈ ℝ^{n+k} and every R ∈ ℝ with B̄_R(y) ⊆ B̄_2(0), the function ρ ↦ ofReal(e^{Λρ}/ρⁿ)·μ(B_ρ(y)) is monotone (nondecreasing) on the open interval (0, R).

Source: step 6 of the selected node's supplied proof (parent 2(a), 2(b)) with Λ := rΛ_K as in its (0c); Simon 7.3.3, proof of (1), uses the monotonicity 4.7 of Ch. 4 for the members of 𝒯 (chapter-07.txt lines 474–483). Positive-scale members are written (a, t) = (z + rx, rλ). Siblings used: zero_limit_minimizing (Submission.dimred_tr_bc_zero_limit_minimizing, with (MB)) and ambient_calculus (Submission.idtp_fons_cc_ambient_calculus) parts (1), (2), (3).
Notation: μ_T := RT.measure, W := B_{2r}(z), K := B̄_{2r}(z), E := ℝ^{n+k}.
1. (Choice of Λ.) K is compact (isCompact_closedBall) and K ⊆ U. Apply (MON) to T with d := n + ℓ (1 ≤ n ≤ n + ℓ ≤ n + k; the other hypotheses are those of T) and part (i) to K: there is Λ_K ≥ 0 such that, whenever B̄_{R′}(c′) ⊆ K, the map τ ↦ ofReal(e^{Λ_Kτ}/τⁿ)·M_{B_τ(c′)}(T) is monotone on (0, R′). Put Λ := rΛ_K ≥ 0.
2. (Products.) If g : ℝ → [0, ∞] is monotone on (0, R) and κ ≥ 0, then ρ ↦ ofReal(e^{κρ})·g(ρ) is monotone on (0, R): both factors are nonnegative and monotone there (mul_le_mul'). For real κ₁, κ₂ and ρ > 0, ofReal(e^{(κ₁+κ₂)ρ}/ρⁿ) = ofReal(e^{κ₁ρ})·ofReal(e^{κ₂ρ}/ρⁿ) (Real.exp_add, ENNReal.ofReal_mul).
3. Let μ ∈ 𝓜, y ∈ E and R ∈ ℝ with B̄_R(y) ⊆ B̄_2(0). If R ≤ 0, then (0, R) = ∅ and there is nothing to prove; assume R > 0. Then ‖y‖ + R ≤ 2: since n + k ≥ 1, there is a unit vector u with y = ‖y‖u (u := ‖y‖⁻¹y if y ≠ 0, any unit vector otherwise); the point y + Ru lies in B̄_R(y) ⊆ B̄_2(0) and has norm ‖y‖ + R.
4. (Case PS.) μ = ofReal(t⁻¹ⁿ) • (μ_T⌞W).map(dilation a t) with 0 < t ≤ r and dist(a, z) ≤ r − t. Put c′ := a + t•y.

 (c) Hence, for 0 < ρ < R, G(ρ) := ofReal(e^{tΛ_Kρ}/ρⁿ)·μ(B_ρ(y)) = ofReal(e^{Λ_K(tρ)}/(tρ)ⁿ)·M_{B_{tρ}(c′)}(T), since ofReal(e^{tΛ_Kρ}/ρⁿ)·ofReal(t⁻¹ⁿ) = ofReal(e^{Λ_K(tρ)}/(tρ)ⁿ) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul, (tρ)ⁿ = tⁿρⁿ). 5. (Case ZS.) μ = RS.measure for an IMRep RS of S in E with zero-scale data (c_i, t_i, b). Then dist(b, z) ≤ r (limit of dist(c_i, z) < r), so b ∈ U, and zero_limit_minimizing (with (MB), the hypotheses of T and x := b) shows that S is minimizing in E with ∂S = 0. Apply (MON) to S with P := n + k, d := n + k and U = N = univ: IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 (n + k) univ by ambient_calculus (1), (closure univ ∖ univ) ∩ univ = ∅, S is minimizing in univ ∩ univ = univ, spt S ⊆ univ ∩ univ, and ∂S = 0. 6. Steps 4 and 5 prove the claim with the single constant Λ = rΛ_K of step 1. ∎

 (a) Put xs := (c_i), lams := (t_i) and hlams := hts. Then xs_i ∈ B_r(z), since dist(c_i, z) < r − t_i < r; lams → 0; and blowUp T xs_i lams_i ⇀ S is part of the data.
